title: RAW input alpha above 1.0 is dropped from expression upon color picker close and clamped to 1.0 upon value refresh
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot v4.6.1.stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Single-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8142) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600X 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.90 GiB memory

### Issue description

Currently, alpha can only be modulated above 1.0 using code or the color picker's RAW input, but the latter is rather unfriendly with how it currently handles values above 1.0. In the example clip I've uploaded, I have a simple scene with a Node2D with a Sprite2D as its child. I decrease the Sprite2D's alpha to make it transparent, then increase the Node2D's alpha to 2.0 to make the Sprite2D fully opaque, then hit enter to confirm my changes. This closes the color picker window, and upon opening it, you can see that the alpha is missing from the expression but still applied. Clicking out of the color picker in this state will preserve the increased alpha, but clicking into any field besides the RAW input field will cause it to reset.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6c8dfa1-dd64-40df-8451-28b66fab465e

Lowering alpha below 1.0 while the RAW input field is open will add alpha as the fourth field, and editing from there works as expected; changing it to any positive value below 1.0 won't cause any issues when closing the color picker or clicking into its fields.

One solution could be always making alpha visible in the RAW input field, or just hiding it if it's not equal to 1.0 or if the user hasn't modified it. Setting alpha above 1.0 has a clear use case in the editor since it can help you visualize how things will look if you're modulating a chain of nodes.

There's an additional issue I considered opening a separate report for that would be largely mitigated if alpha were always available in the RAW input field; that being that attempting to input a space into the field immediately closes the color picker and discards your input. The expression present in the field follows Godot's style guide and has spaces between its values, but anyone trying to follow suit by putting a space before their alpha value might come to the mistaken conclusion that editing alpha with the field isn't possible to begin with.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open color picker on any node
2. Switch to RAW input mode
3. Drag the alpha slider below to make an alpha value appear or type in your own and make it higher than 1.0
4. Press enter to confirm
5. Re-open color picker and check RAW input field to see that your value is no longer visible
6. Click into any field besides RAW input to see your change reverted

N/A
